_comment: Term policy for Urdu audio translation, as data rather than prose buried in a workflow prompt. Read by --assemble-urdu for normalisation, and pasted into the translation prompt so both stages agree. The v1 translation transliterated everything into Urdu script and 'acks' became ایکس, which the ur-PK voice reads as the letter X. Technical vocabulary now stays in Latin script.

policy.keepLatin: All technical vocabulary, product names and config keys stay in Latin script, spelled as in the English source. The Urdu voice pronounces them correctly; transliterating them does not.
policy.translate: Everything else - connecting prose, verbs, explanations, reasoning - becomes Urdu script.
policy.result: Urdu sentence structure carrying English technical terms, which is how this is actually explained in Pakistani engineering teams.

_spacedAcronyms: Written with spaces so the voice reads them as letters rather than attempting a word.
_headings: Twelve parallel translators produced three different words for 'Section' (حصہ / سیکشن / Section) and mixed digits with Urdu numerals. Normalised automatically by --assemble-urdu; do not rely on the translators agreeing.
_markers: Must survive translation exactly. '-- think --' is the gap where the listener attempts a drill question; dropping it destroys the exercise. Counts are checked against the English sidecar and a mismatch fails the build.
_transliterated: English words spelled phonetically in Urdu letters. The voice reads Urdu letters, so it cannot pronounce these as the English words they are -- which is the whole bug this pipeline exists to fix. Keys are the Urdu-script spelling, values the English word that should have been left in Latin script. Checked by --assemble-urdu; a hit fails the build. Add entries as you hear new ones. Note that a REAL Urdu word is fine (dastavez for document is correct Urdu and pronounces correctly); only phonetic renderings of English belong here.
